The '''Brass Soldiers of Axum''' were a<ref name="TEA" /> mysterious<ref name="Centerpoint">{{SW|url=news/the-world-puller-the-history-of-centerpoint-station-needs-author-entry|text=Galactic Architecture 101 and the History of Centerpoint Station|int=Galactic Architecture 101 and the History of Centerpoint Station|nolive=1}}</ref> collection of thirty-five thousand statues of [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]]. They were cast in solid [[Brass/Legends|brass]] and depicted the soldiers with expressions of pain and terror. The Brass Soldiers of Axum shared their name with [[Axum]], a [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] and once-[[Capital/Legends|capital]] of the [[Azure Imperium]] state that predated the [[Galactic Constitution Conference|formation]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="TEA" />

According to legend, the statues originated as an actual pre-Republic [[Army/Legends|army]] that was transmuted into brass via [[Magic/Legends|magic]].<ref name="TEA" /> Eventually, the Brass Soldiers of Axum were included in the [[Twenty Wonders of the Galaxy]]&mdash;a list of spectactular, antique artificial objects that the [[Historian/Legends|historian]] [[Vicendi]] compiled in [[10,000 BBY]] for the publication ''[[Arturum Galactinum]]''.<ref name="TEA" /> At some point between [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]] and [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="Jewel dates">{{JewelofYavindate}}</ref> a pair of life-size replicas of the brass statues flanked the entrance of "[[Wonders of the Galaxy (exhibit)|Wonders of the Galaxy]]," an exhibit of the [[Figg & Associates Art Museum]] in the [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]] [[City/Legends|settlement]] of the<ref name="Jewel">''[[The Jewel of Yavin]]''</ref> [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] planet [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]].<ref name="TEA" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Clearly a gloss on the famous Terracotta Army of Qin Shi Huang. I rather like the idea that these are actual soldiers transformed into brass statues through magic, but I left it vague.|Daniel Wallace|<ref name="Blog">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2009/08/endnotes-for-star-wars-essential-atlas_24.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for Star Wars: The Essential Atlas (part 2 of 5)}}</ref>}}
[[File:Essential_Atlas.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Brass Soldiers of Axum were created for ''The Essential Atlas''.]]
The Brass Soldiers of Axum were introduced in the [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' by [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Jason Fry]].<ref name="TEA" /> Wallace noted in his personal blog that he particularly enjoyed creating names for those of the Twenty Wonders of the Galaxy that were original to the book, which included the brass soldiers.<ref name="Blog" />

The author remarked that the Brass Soldiers of Axum were based on the famous real-world [[Wikipedia:Terracotta Army|Terracotta Army]] of [[Wikipedia:Qin Shi Huang|Qin Shi Huang]]. In addition, Wallace noted that he enjoyed the idea of the Brass Soldiers having originally been living beings that were magically transformed into statues, but he opted to leave their origin uncertain<ref name="Blog" /> by presenting it as an [[in-universe]] legend.<ref name="TEA" /> The Brass Soldiers of Axum made their first appearance in the form of replicas in ''[[The Jewel of Yavin]]'', a [[2014]] adventure supplement for [[Fantasy Flight Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: Edge of the Empire]]'' [[Star Wars Roleplaying|roleplaying game]] system.<ref name="Jewel" />
